routes.reason: Part II of RefinedTraceMethods for the henselian-pair rigidity theorem and its machinery (84 items). The title reproduces the parent's atlas title 'Hochschild, cyclotomic and refined trace methods' exactly, the area ktheory is a galaxy id, and the brief is 863 words that name the theorems and the imports. RT.3 owns the Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem and RT.2 the cyclotomic spectra this rests on, but neither plans the finiteness of TC/p, nonunital henselian rings, pseudocoherent functors or the pro Geisser–Levine theorem, so a Part II rather than a stage is right. The same id and title are already used by PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 and PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21, so this extraction joins an existing proposal instead of opening a parallel one.

Part II of RefinedTraceMethods for §5.2's continuity theorems, joining the proposal PAPER-ANTIEAU-MATHEW-MORROW-ETAL-22 made under the same id and title. Its brief already asks for continuous invariants F^cts(X) = lim F(X_n) and for the comparison maps that are p-adic equivalences, which is exactly Theorems 5.19–5.22 here, so one owner for p-adic continuity is right. Accepted with the area corrected: 'motivic' is the parent's atlas group, not a galaxy id, and the value is now 'ktheory', as in route 1.

New roadmap ArcTopologyAndDescent for Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change, the single item. The id, title and area etale are the ones PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21 (122 items), PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17, PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24 and PAPER-GUO-REINECKE-24 already use, so this route contributes one source statement to a roadmap another extraction owns rather than proposing a second one; its 79-word brief is short for that reason and says so.

Source of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 for the equivalent characterizations of henselian pairs, henselization of pairs, Elkik's theorem and Néron–Popescu — Stacks-project commutative algebra of exactly the kind SF.0 already receives from the Česnavičius extraction.

Source of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 for Kunz's finiteness of F-finite rings, F-finiteness of henselizations and regularity of completions of excellent rings. R03.3 is where excellence and catenarity hypotheses for local rings live, and the Bhatt–Mathew syntomic extraction routes the same kind of statement there.

Source of DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 for finite generation of the homotopy of the cotangent complex for F-finite rings and dim Ω¹_k = log_p[k : k^p] via p-bases. DD.0 owns cotangent complexes and Kähler differentials, which is what both statements are about.

Source of CrystallineCohomology CR.4 for Illusie I.5.7 for logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves and Shiho's extension to regular F_p-schemes. CR.4 owns classical de Rham–Witt theory of smooth and, through Popescu, regular F_p-algebras.

Source of RefinedTraceMethods RT.2 for Hesselholt's HKR theorem for TR of smooth F_p-algebras. CR.4 assigns the THH/TR realization of de Rham–Witt to RefinedTraceMethods and RT.2 plans the agreement with the classical TR/TC formulation, so the realization statement belongs there and not with the de Rham–Witt complex itself.

Source of RefinedTraceMethods RT.3 for the Cortiñas–Geisser–Hesselholt–Land–Tamme excision theorem for K^inv. RT.3 lists excision among the named inputs of the relative K/TC comparison, and this is that input in its general form.

notes: Accept, with one correction in place. Both recorded hashes reproduce: the arXiv v2 PDF (ad23c1d7…) and the e-print tarball (22f7d57f…), whose rigidity_final.tex is 4016 lines as recorded, so every quotation below is checked against the authors' own source rather than against an extraction of the PDF. Structure: 122 items (103 missing, 18 planned, 1 library), every missing item routed exactly once, no route takes a planned or library item, all six source stage ids exist, all 18 planned layer ids exist, both Part II titles reproduce the parent's atlas title exactly, and check_paper.py passes. Coverage: 159 numbered environments appear in the PDF text and every one of them is in an item — the four my checker flagged are false alarms (Definition 2.2 is inside item 013 'Definitions 2.1–2.3', Example 2.17 inside item 027 'Examples 2.16–2.18', Theorem 5.21 is item 096, and the 'Remark 4.38' on p.5 is a cross-reference, not a declaration). Locators: 170 name-and-page checks land on exactly the page given; the handful that did not are proofs spanning a page boundary (Theorem 5.7 stated p.39, proof pp.40–41; Example 6.10 opening on p.53) or my own parsing of 'Definition 3.1, Examples 3.2–3.3' style lists. Statuses: the library item's three declarations are at Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean — HenselianRing:94, HenselianLocalRing:108, and IsAdicComplete.henselianRing:170, which the regex index does not list because it is declared as 'instance (priority := 100)' and which I therefore read in the source. I sampled the planned targets, including the two that look surprising: the Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 4D does own 'strict henselisation and completion of strict henselisations', and ALS.2 is the Borel–Serre compactification that gives finiteness of classifying spaces of congruence subgroups. The correction is route 2's area, 'motivic', which is the parent roadmap's atlas group and not a galaxy id in data/galaxies.json; it is now 'ktheory', matching route 1's Part II of the same parent. This is worth the maintainer's attention beyond this file: 33 of the 502 route areas across research/blueprint/papers carry group names rather than galaxy ids (modular 15, cohomology 7, motivic 4, algebra 4, and one each of classical, diophantine and numbertheory), and scripts/check_paper.py does not validate the field, which is why they pass. In particular PAPER-ANTIEAU-MATHEW-MORROW-ETAL-22 proposes this same roadmap id with the same invalid area and needs the same fix in its own review; I did not touch that file. All seven findings are confirmed against the TeX source: the duplicated \cite{GH} at line 397 with GH = [30] and GL = [34] in the .bbl (E1); (Law) asking for a left adjoint and the next sentence calling it a right adjoint (E2); the three slips and the index shift in the proof of Theorem 5.7, where the Bloch–Esnault–Kerz bound at the corrected index costs at most a factor C(2j+2,2j)/C(2j,2j−2) ≤ 6 (E3); {R^{r−s}}_s in the proof of Lemma 5.30 against {R^{s−r}}_s in its statement (E4); 'we can assume x^*α = 0' where the statement to be proved is that x^*α is independent of x, so the normalization that is available is x_0^*α = 0 (E5); K(O_C; Z_p) ≃ K(C; C_p) (E6); and π_{n+1}(𝒯𝒞/p^r) described as the sheafification of π_n (E7). Nothing else was corrected, rejected or deleted, and I add no finding: I read the source around each finding and the statements the routes cite, not all 4016 lines. The published JAMS text was not compared here either; it returns 403, as the extraction records, and Crossref registers no correction for 10.1090/jams/961.
